resolved.item: Justice and righteousness (Rom 5:16, Acts 24:25 as Greek examples)
resolved.note: All four examples are now Hebrew 'justice and righteousness' verses, and the Greek 'judgment' verses have their own row, Righteousness and judgment. Minor: the four are two parallel pairs (1 Chr 18:14 = 2 Sam 8:15; 1 Kgs 10:9 = 2 Chr 9:8), so Gen 18:19 or Amos 5:24 would show more.

resolved.item: The righteousness of the LORD, of God (first-match pull, cross-row, misfits)
resolved.note: Rom 1:17, 3:22 and Phil 3:9 now stand in both this row and the faith row, and the note is kept. 1 John 3:10, Deut 9:4 and Isa 48:1 are out. Deut 9:6 (not because of your righteousness) is still in the row, and a few other members do not state a righteousness of the LORD (see new items).

resolved.item: Righteousness and faith (Acts 17:31; virtue lists; Gen 15:6 lead; order against law)
resolved.note: Acts 17:31 is out. The 'credited as righteousness' row now carries Gen 15:6, Rom 4 and Gal 3:6, and double membership removes the order problem. But 1 Tim 6:11 and 2 Tim 2:22 are still in the row and are two of the four examples shown (with Matt 21:32 and 2 Pet 1:1), so the shown examples are pursue-it lists, not the faith-and-righteousness verses. Show Rom 4:3, Gal 3:6 or Rom 1:17 instead.

resolved.item: Righteousness and the law (order; commandment companion; Deut 6:25)
resolved.note: Deut 6:25 leads, Ps 119 verses and 2 Pet 2:21 are caught, and the shared-verse note plus double membership puts Rom 10:4-6, Gal 3:6 and Phil 3:9 in both rows.

resolved.item: Seek, pursue, hunger for it (Matt 5:10, Prov 11:19, missing pursue verses)
resolved.note: Matt 5:10 and Prov 11:19 are out, and Matt 5:6, Matt 6:33, Prov 15:9, Prov 21:21, 1 Tim 6:11, 2 Tim 2:22 and Rom 9:30 are in. Rom 9:31 ('pursued a law of righteousness') was not brought across; it went to the persecuted row instead (see new items).
1 Kgs 8:32 is out; the examples are all human practice.

resolved.item: Righteousness and sin (anomia and rish'ah under 'sin')
resolved.note: Relabelled 'Righteousness and sin, wickedness', so 2 Cor 6:14 and Deut 9:5 now sit under a label that names them.

Relabelled 'faithfulness and loving devotion', which fixes Ps 103:17 and Hos 10:12. Zech 8:8, Jer 4:2, Ps 119:142 and Isa 59:14 are still in the row only by 'truth' (emet), which the label does not name, and no row note lists the three words.

resolved.item: The righteous and the wicked (several words; Rom 5:19 and 1 Pet 3:18 placed by first-match)
resolved.note: Relabelled 'the wicked, the unrighteous, sinners', and Rom 5:19 has its own row. But 1 Pet 3:18 ('Christ, the righteous for the unrighteous') is still the third of four examples in the general moral-contrast row, as well as in the Jesus row. Use a different example here.

resolved.item: Called righteous (177 mixed verses; denials; Christ)
resolved.note: Now split into The LORD is righteous, Jesus called righteous (by hand), Made righteous, the righteous/wicked row, and 'Who else is called righteous, and who is not'. The denials (Rom 3:10, Eccl 7:20) are not set apart inside the last row, and that row still holds God-is-righteous verses (see new items).

resolved.item: Justified, and faith (Jas 2:24 and Gal 2:16 placement; Acts 13:38; 1 Tim 3:16)
resolved.note: Verses naming faith and works are in both rows (Rom 3:28, 4:5, Gal 2:16, Jas 2:24). Acts 13:39 is corrected and 1 Tim 3:16 is out. Note kept.

resolved.item: Justified, and works (Matt 11:19; James as the exception)
resolved.note: Matt 11:19 is out, and Jas 2:21, 24, 25 are now in the row. But all four examples shown are Pauline (Rom 3:20, 3:28, 4:2, 4:5), so a Catholic, Orthodox or Wesleyan reader first sees only 'not by works' in a row labelled 'and works'. Show Jas 2:24 as an example.

resolved.note: The label is now neutral ('Every other use: justified, in the right, vindicated'). But the shown examples lead with 1 Kgs 8:32, Luke 10:29 and 1 Cor 4:4, while Rom 3:24, 5:9, 8:30 and Titus 3:7 are only in the verse list, and 'every other use' sets Rom 3:24 beside Luke 10:29. Lead with Rom 3:24, 5:9 and 8:30.

resolved.item: Missing: credited wording; tsedeq noun verses; clothing
resolved.note: 'Credited as righteousness' is a row of its own (11 verses), Ps 89:14, 97:2 and 23:3 are placed, and 'Clothed in righteousness' exists.
Neither verse appears in any listed row; presumably still in 'More'. Optional: a small row 'Jesus speaks of righteousness' if the text allows.

new.why: The row seems to be filled by the Greek dioko, which means both 'pursue' and 'persecute'. Phil 3:6 has Paul persecuting the church, the opposite of the label. Rom 9:31 is Israel pursuing a law of righteousness and not attaining it, which has no suffering in it. Two of the four verses shown (half the row) do not show the label.
new.fix: Remove both from this row. Put Rom 9:31 in 'Seek, pursue, hunger for it' beside Rom 9:30 and leave Phil 3:6 in the law row. That leaves Matt 5:10 and 1 Pet 3:14, so fold the row into 'Righteousness and sin' or drop it.

new.row: Who else is called righteous, and who is not
new.why: 'Else' means other than the LORD and Jesus, but two of the four shown examples are about God or Christ (1 John 1:9 'He is faithful and just'; 1 John 2:29 'He is righteous') and the row holds the main 'God is righteous' verses that 'The LORD is righteous' (9 verses) lacks. That leaves the God row thin and mislabels the rest. 1 John 2:29, where 'He' may be the Father or Christ, is a divine-person placement made by a rule here.
new.fix: Place the God-is-righteous verses by hand into 'The LORD is righteous' (Deut 32:4, Ps 119:137, Lam 1:18, Ezra 9:15, Neh 9:8, Rev 15:3, 16:5, 16:7, 1 John 1:9) and decide 1 John 2:29 by hand. Show people (Gen 6:9, Luke 1:6, Acts 10:22) and a denial (Rom 3:10) as the shown examples.

new.why: The second shown example reads 'in holiness and righteousness before Him all the days of our lives' and has no salvation or deliverance word in it, so the example does not show the label.
new.fix: Swap for Ps 98:2, Ps 71:2 or Isa 59:17, or add a note that the companion is in the neighbouring verse.

new.why: The verse as shown ends at 'breastplate of righteousness arrayed' and does not contain peace; peace is in v15. The same verse is in the faith row and its faith is in v16, so the window runs across verses.
new.fix: Swap for Ps 85:10 or Jas 3:18 as the shown example, and say in a note when a companion sits in the next verse.

new.why: Shown as the second example, but the text ('king of righteousness ... king of Salem means king of peace') has no deliverance or life. It is also an odd neighbour of Ezek 14:14 in a row that is about whether righteousness saves.
new.fix: Replace with Prov 11:4 or Prov 12:28 as the shown example; keep Heb 7:2 only in the peace row.

new.why: 'Preacher of righteousness' with the flood: the verse as shown contains no judge, judgment or justice word (the judgment word is in v4), so the shown example does not display the companion.
new.fix: Show 2 Tim 4:8 and Acts 24:25 first, and drop 2 Pet 2:5 from the shown set.

new.why: Rom 4:25 ('raised to life for our justification') has no 'credited' and no faith in it, yet it is in this row (and in the faith row). This row is the one place a reader will take 'credited' literally.
new.fix: Remove Rom 4:25 from this row and from the faith row, or leave it in Justified/justification with a note.

new.why: It is the first example, and the BSB text shown reads 'innocent man', so a reader looking for 'righteous' sees none. The original has dikaios, in brackets, but the first line of a hand-picked row should show the label.
new.fix: Lead with Acts 3:14, Acts 7:52 and Acts 22:14 ('the Righteous One'), and add a short note on Matt 27:19: 'Greek dikaios; the BSB renders innocent.'

new.why: A one-verse row headed 'Made righteous' (shown as '1 verses') puts the translation's word 'made' (Greek: constituted, set down as) as the label, beside 'Credited' above, with no note. Lutheran/Reformed and Catholic/Orthodox/Wesleyan readers each read that word differently, and the row presents the BSB reading as the text's.
new.fix: Fix '1 verse', and add the same sort of note the God and justified rows have: 'the Greek verb here is kathistemi (constituted, set down as); readers part on whether this is declared or imparted, and the page takes no side.' Or fold the row into the righteous/wicked row.

new.row: The righteousness of the LORD, of God
new.why: Besides Deut 9:6, these two do not state a righteousness of the LORD. Isa 61:3 is 'oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD' and Isa 51:1 is 'you who pursue righteousness, who seek the LORD', so the row is still partly filled by the word God occurring in the verse, as in the first review.
new.fix: Remove Isa 61:3, Isa 51:1 and Deut 9:6; Isa 51:1 belongs in the seek row, where it already is.

summary: Most of the first review's problems are resolved: the double membership, the credited row, the corrected labels, the Jesus row and the new justice and throne rows all work. What remains is small: several shown examples do not display their row's label (Phil 3:6 and Rom 9:31 in the persecuted row, Luke 1:75, Eph 6:14, Heb 7:2, 2 Pet 2:5, Rom 4:25, Matt 27:19), the 'Who else' row still holds God-is-righteous verses, and the faith and works rows show pursue-lists or Pauline verses first.
